validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/DUPLICATE/ATTRIBUTION-BASELINE check. Northstar Gas Pipeline is a real, independently documented facility: Alaska DNR's Division of Oil & Gas maintains a live registry page for it (Status: Active), and three Petroleum News articles from 2000 (contemporaneous trade press, independent of GEM and of the DNR page) describe its construction and 2000 startup carrying gas to Northstar Island for BP's NorthStar Unit development. Checked the roster of 42 in-scope Alaska/Northeast pipelines (P7450-P7465 and siblings) for a duplicate/relabel candidate: found none -- Northstar Gas is BP/Harvest Alaska's single dedicated gas line serving Northstar Island, distinct in name, geometry, and function from the other Alaska rows in this batch (no other roster row references Northstar Island, NorthStar Unit, or Harvest Alaska's Northstar system). Ownership chain independently confirmed: BP Exploration (Alaska) Inc. developed and originally operated the line (per the 2000-2001 Petroleum News articles); BP transferred its NorthStar pipeline interests to Harvest Alaska, LLC in 2014 (DNR page: 'On May 29, 2014, BP requested that DNR approve a transfer...to Harvest Alaska, LLC'), consistent with Harvest Alaska (a Hilcorp subsidiary) being the current Operator/Owner1 on the sheet. No evidence found that this pipeline should not exist as its own tracked row, and no candidate duplicate identified.

validity.recommendation: consider correcting Diameter from 10.15 to 10 (in); DiameterUnits unaffected
validity.researcher_notes: This is the batch's flagged Diameter anomaly. Alaska DNR's OWN page contradicts itself: its structured field reads 'Diameters (in): 10.15' (an exact match to GEM's recorded value -- strongly suggesting GEM copied this field verbatim, artifact and all), while the SAME page's prose independently and TWICE states the diameter is 10-inch: 'Harvest Alaska, LLC, operates the 10-inch oil pipeline and 10-inch gas pipeline that extend into the Beaufort Sea to the gravel island.' No occurrence of the substring '15' appears anywhere in the prose, and neither of the two hypotheses floated in the batch guidance is supported by the text: there is no second, larger-diameter segment described anywhere ('10, 15' as two concatenated diameters), and the field is not obviously a decimal-comma artifact of a metric conversion either (10.15 in is not a clean conversion of any round metric diameter). The simplest reading is that the DNR web form's 'Diameters (in)' field independently mis-renders/mis-concatenates data for the two colocated NorthStar pipelines (the 10-inch oil line and the 10-inch gas line entered in this dataset) into a single '10.15' string, while the hand-written prose summary on the same page was written correctly. No SECOND, independent origin was found stating a diameter at all (Petroleum News, AOGCC 2004, Hilcorp/Harvest corporate sites all silent on pipe diameter) -- so this remains a single-origin internal contradiction, not a two-source disagreement, and is deliberately staged as a 'concern' rather than an outright value change. Tier reflects that this rests on one document's own internal consistency, not corroboration.

validity.recommendation: verify whether StartLocation/EndLocation (and the paired District/State/Country columns) should be swapped -- gas appears to flow FROM the Central Gas Facility TO Northstar Island, opposite the sheet's current Start=Northstar Island/End=Central Gas Facility
validity.researcher_notes: Two INDEPENDENT origins describe this gas line's function and direction as shore-to-island, not island-to-shore: (1) Alaska DNR's own page: 'Harvest Alaska, LLC, operates the 10-inch oil pipeline and 10-inch gas pipeline that extend into the Beaufort Sea to the gravel island' -- i.e. the pipelines run FROM the mainland/shore infrastructure TO the island. (2) Petroleum News, 'BP begins shipping natural gas to Northstar' (Oct 28, 2000): 'BP Exploration (Alaska) Inc. began to move natural gas to Northstar Island in October...' -- explicitly gas moving TO the island. This matches Northstar Island's own well-documented engineering history (checked via Wikipedia strictly as a LEADS source, never cited): the gas line's purpose was to deliver gas FROM shore facilities TO the island for reservoir re-pressurization/gas-lift, the opposite function from an oil-export line (which runs island-to-shore). If GEM's Start/End convention records the pipeline's flow origin as 'Start' and destination as 'End', the sheet's current Start=Northstar Island/End=Central Gas Facility appears to have the direction reversed for this specific gas line (as opposed to the co-located Northstar OIL pipeline, which correctly runs island-to-shore and for which this Start/End assignment would be right). Not changed outright here because (a) I could not independently confirm GEM's own Start/End convention rule for gas-lift/injection lines specifically, and (b) 'Central Gas Facility' as an exact named endpoint was not independently verified in either source (DNR and Petroleum News describe the mainland-side infrastructure only generically). Two distinct, independently verified origins (Alaska DNR; Petroleum News) agree on the shore-to-island direction, supporting tier high for the underlying direction fact even though the exact Start/End field correction is left to a human reviewer's judgment on GEM's convention.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Alaska DNR's Division of Oil & Gas Northstar Gas registry page is a LIVE, current public record (fetched 2026-09-14) and states 'Status: Active' with Harvest Alaska, LLC as the current operator and no 'Related Documents' indicating a shutdown, sale-in-progress-only, or abandonment filing since the 2014 BP-to-Harvest transfer. No news, DNR notice, or RCA/AOGCC filing found indicating the line has since been shut in, released, or abandoned (the only DNR-hosted document found, the 2017 Partial Release of Interest, narrows the right-of-way footprint but explicitly continues to identify Harvest Alaska as 'Owner and Operator' -- a partial ROW release, not an operational status change). Confirmed 'operating' as recorded. Only one verified origin (Alaska DNR) speaks to CURRENT status specifically (Petroleum News sources are all dated 2000-2001 and speak only to historical construction/startup, not current status), so tier is medium; independent=false. Not a dormancy case (proposed/shelved/cancelled inference rules do not apply -- this is a recorded 'operating' row with a live, current confirming source, not a stalled proposal).

summary: P7463 Northstar Gas Pipeline (Harvest Alaska LLC, North Slope AK): existence/classification/duplicate-baseline confirmed (caveat) via Alaska DNR's live registry page + 3 independent 2000-era Petroleum News articles -- no duplicate found among the 42-row Alaska/Northeast roster. Investigated the batch's flagged Diameter anomaly: staged as a SPEC concern -- DNR's own page internally contradicts itself (structured field '10.15' vs. prose '10-inch' stated twice), recommend considering Diameter=10; kept recorded 10.15 in the fill pending a human call, single-origin so tier medium there. Raised a second concern (ATTRIBUTION): DNR prose + Petroleum News both independently describe gas flowing FROM shore TO Northstar Island, opposite the sheet's Start=Northstar Island/End=Central Gas Facility -- flagged at tier high (2 distinct origins) but left the Start/End field values unchanged pending a human ruling on GEM's own Start/End convention for injection/lift lines. All 15 worklist units filled: Status/Fuel/Length/FuelSource/Location REFS_ADDED or REVERIFIED at tier medium (Alaska DNR is the only verified origin after ruling out NPMS [navigation-only, no name match] and the RCA news item [Wayback-recovered but about unrelated BP-Hilcorp dockets, not Northstar]); Construction and Start reached tier HIGH/independent via a second, genuinely independent origin (Petroleum News, 3 articles = one origin) corroborating DNR's dates, with a minor Start-date discrepancy noted (PN: gas moving Oct 2000; DNR: construction-dates range ending 01/01/2001) but not treated as a contradiction. Operator (previously MISSING_REF) and Owner both sourced to Alaska DNR (registry page + a scanned Partial-Release PDF hand-OCR'd after url_verifier's automated check failed on it) -- both count as ONE origin per this addendum's agency-page-plus-hosted-document rule, so tier medium/independent false there despite two distinct URLs. UNRESOLVED (tier low, nothing found despite searching DNR, all 3 Petroleum News articles, AOGCC 2004 [zero Northstar mentions despite being a Wikipedia footnote], Hilcorp/Harvest corporate sites, guessed BOEM URLs [all 404], and the EIA pipeline-projects CSV [no match]): ProposalYear/Month, Capacity, Pressure, SegmentCost. PipelineType (transmission) also UNRESOLVED as a value-confirmation matter -- no source uses GEM's controlled vocabulary for this line -- but see the attribution concern above questioning whether it fits 'transmission' at all given its apparent injection/lift-gas function. Status review: confirm 'operating' (DNR's live registry, tier medium, single origin).
